answer: Each agent publishes a signed beacon tied to a hardware‑bound kernel identifier that only a trusted enclave can generate. When a new node requests grading rights, a falcon‑speed verification routine checks the beacon against a distributed ledger; mismatches trigger a honeypot challenge that forces the claimant to solve a computational puzzle and reveal its unique enclave proof. An attacker must fabricate dozens of hardware‑rooted kernels and solve thousands of puzzles, inflating cost to billions of CPU cycles and rendering Sybil attacks economically infeasible.
